text:
PhaseNet via SeisBench, run on continuous waveforms downloaded from EarthScope, GEOFON, and Raspberry Shake FDSN. Code lives in ~/Documents/bransfield-eq/ .
| Network | Stations | Data center | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| ZX | 14 ( BRA13 – BRA27 ) | EarthScope | BRAVOSEIS OBS, low-gain ?L? |
| ZX | 8 ( BRA02–05, 08–11 ) | GEOFON ( GFZ ) | BRAVOSEIS OBS, high-gain BB HH? @ 100 Hz |
| 5M | 14 (Bransfield bbox) | GEOFON ( GFZ ) | reused temp code — bbox filter |
| AI.JUBA | 1 | EarthScope | Antarctic permanent |
| AM.R4DE2 | 1 | Raspberry Shake | bbox filter (epochs reused) |
[!warning] BRAVOSEIS OBS split across two data centers — and two instrument types
EarthScope (BRA13-27) hosts low-gain seismometers with mixed sample rates (200 Hz Z, 100 Hz horizontals, 200 Hz hydrophone).
GEOFON (BRA02-11) hosts high-gain broadband at uniform 100 Hz ( HHZ/HH1/HH2 ).
Picker handles both — resamples to 100 Hz before PhaseNet — but discrimination/location may need to treat them separately for noise floor reasons.
Window: 2019-01-01 → 2020-03-01 (BRAVOSEIS deployment + a 2-month tail).
Bbox (Bransfield): lat -65 to -60, lon -65 to -54.
The BRAVOSEIS OBS uses low-gain seismometer code, not high-gain. Initial channel filter EH?,HH?,BH?,SH? returned zero for ZX. Actual ZX seismic channels:
ELZ @ 200 Hz — short-period low-gain vertical
SL1 , SL2 @ 100 Hz — short-period low-gain horizontals
EDH @ 200 Hz — hydrophone (skipped for picking)
Final channel glob (covers all our targets):
EH?,HH?,BH?,SH?,EL?,HL?,BL?,SL?
[!warning] Sample-rate mismatch on ZX
Vertical is 200 Hz, horizontals are 100 Hz on the same station. PhaseNet expects 3C aligned at one sample rate (default 100 Hz). Plan: downsample Z to 100 Hz at picking time (SeisBench does this if you set sampling_rate=100 ), but verify on a single trace first.

sectionTitle: Disk-space budget — how it was derived
sectionPath: Disk-space budget — how it was derived
text:
Estimate uses actual operational overlap of each channel-epoch with the window, multiplied by the channel's sample rate, then divided by a Steim2 compression ratio of 3.5.
bytes_in_window = sample_rate_hz * 4 * overlap_seconds / 3.5
Initial naïve estimate (every channel-epoch × full year) gave ~2 TB and was wrong because:
ZX BRA* filter was needed — the unfiltered ZX network spans 2003-2022 and includes a New Zealand deployment in 2021/2022.
Channel-epochs are short snippets (response changes), not deployment-long.
5M includes European stations under the same temp code.
Channel filter excludes SOH ( ACE , LCE , LCQ , ...) and hydrophone.
Final estimate (seismic 3C + hydrophone, BRAVOSEIS window, all filters applied):
| Net | Stations | GB |
|---|---|---|
| ZX (EarthScope, 14 stations + GEOFON, 8 stations) | 22 | 460 (incl. hydrophone on EarthScope subset) |
| 5M | 14 | 85 |
| AI | 1 | 15 |
| AM (R4DE2) | 1 | 0.1 (only 5 days of true Bransfield data) |
| Total | 38 | ~560 GB |
Budget ~1.4 TB free disk (2.5× for raw + working copies + pick CSVs). Laptop can't host this — running on a cluster with a scratch volume.
| Network | Client |
|---|---|
| ZX, AI | Client("EARTHSCOPE") |
| 5M | Client("GFZ") (GEOFON) |
| AM | Client("https://data.raspberryshake.org") |
EarthScope token / authentication: assumed pre-configured on the run machine. Not yet tested for embargo on ZX — if download fails for ZX , that's the first thing to check.

scripts/02_download_waveforms.py :
One MSEED file per (station, day). Idempotent — file existence = "done".
Empty days written as 0-byte sentinel so 204 responses aren't retried forever.
--shard I --of N partitions the (station × day) Cartesian product across N workers — drop into a SLURM array job.
Per-channel bulk request expands the channel glob server-side.
3 retries with 10 s backoff for transient FDSN failures.
scripts/03_run_phasenet.py :
SeisBench PhaseNet with pretrained weights (start with stead ; cross-check with instance and ethz ).
Per station-day file: read → merge gaps → resample to 100 Hz → model.classify(stream) → write picks CSV.
Parameters to tune: P_threshold , S_threshold (defaults 0.3 / 0.3), blinding , overlap .
Outputs: time, station, network, phase, prob, model_weights .

instance weights (trained on European OBS data) outperform stead (land-only) substantially on Bransfield OBS. Both recall and precision improved — domain match is the right lever, not threshold-tuning alone. Defaults locked in 03_run_phasenet.py and slurm/pick.sbatch .

Download: 1.66 GB MSEED.

sectionTitle: PhaseNet caught a second event at +24 s — validation win
sectionPath: PhaseNet caught a second event at +24 s — validation win
text:
[!note] Not necessarily an "aftershock"
Earlier framing called this an aftershock; without magnitudes or locations that's overclaiming. More likely swarm pair for Bransfield's rift+volcanic context. Pin down via Stage 4 magnitudes + locations + waveform CC.
A 4-station cluster fired at 23:51:34–36 (~25 s after the 23:51:10 manual event 2 on Dec 26):
| Station | P | S | S-P |
|---|---|---|---|
| BRA19 | 23:51:34.74 | 23:51:35.33 | 0.59 s |
| BRA21 | 23:51:35.03 | — | — |
| BRA22 | 23:51:35.27 | 23:51:36.11 | 0.84 s |
| BRA20 | 23:51:35.96 | 23:51:36.02 | 0.06 s ⚠ spurious S |
S-P times of 0.6–0.8 s on BRA19/BRA22 are consistent with a local source ~5 km away — same order as event 2's BRA20 S-P of 0.98 s. Two separate events , close in time and space; not coda of event 2 (24 s gap is far too long for a local source).
Significance:
Genuine event the manual analyst either missed or merged with event 2 — demonstrates the value of running PhaseNet over the full record, not just QA against a manual catalog.
4 stations × right at PyOcto's typical association minimum → would be picked up downstream as a distinct event. Won't be lost.
instance
 weights are 
less
 confident than 
stead
 was on this borderline event (BRA19 P prob 0.97 → 0.34). For marginal events, an ensemble of stead + instance may add real signal. Revisit if Stage 2 / Stage 3 see many borderline events.

Idempotent: skip-if-exists at file granularity (MSEED for downloads, CSV for picks). Configuration consolidated in configs/targets.yaml so window/channels/targets aren't duplicated across scripts. Resampling decision: pick at 100 Hz (PhaseNet default). 200 Hz channels (ZX ELZ , EDH ) are downsampled in the picker via tr.resample(100) . This avoids the 200/100 Hz cross-component mismatch on ZX OBS but means we lose high-frequency content on the vertical — flag this if local micro-events are missed.

Station geometry extracted with scripts/04_station_geometry.py → catalogs/station_geometry.csv . BRAVOSEIS OBS sit at 1019–1495 m water depth; StationXML elevation is reliably negative for OBS, so we have water depth without GEBCO. Land stations have elevation ≥ 0.
AM.R4DE2 epoch trap (resolved) — R4DE2 is a single Raspberry Shake station code that has been physically relocated multiple times. Within our 2019-01 → 2020-03 window it has three epochs: Uruguay (2019-08 to 2020-01-20), Bransfield (2020-01-20 to 2020-01-23, ~3 days at -62.18°/-58.89°), Uruguay again (2020-01-23 to 2020-02-18), Bransfield again (2020-02-18 to 2020-02-20, ~2 days). Solution: enabled bbox_filter: true for AM in targets.yaml . The Raspberry Shake FDSN server filters by channel-epoch coordinates, so only the ~5 days of Bransfield data are returned (~0.1 GB). After 2020-08 R4DE2 has been continuously in Bransfield through 2025; if we ever extend the window past Mar 2020 we get years of permanent Raspberry Shake data .
Refactored 01_data_inventory.py to read from configs/targets.yaml so window/channels/bbox aren't duplicated across scripts. 04_station_geometry.py reads StationXML written by 01_* and adds water_depth_m for OBS.

Multi-class classification of the Stage 1 pick stream. Bransfield Basin sits at an active spreading rift adjacent to glaciated landmasses (Antarctic Peninsula, South Shetland Islands), so non-tectonic seismicity is abundant and scientifically interesting . We catalog both tectonic earthquakes and icequakes; we drop everything else.
| Class | Catalog? | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| tectonic | ✅ keep, primary catalog | Local + regional EQs; the Stage 3-6 inputs |
| icequake | ✅ keep, separate catalog | Calving, basal slip, ice-shelf flexure, glacial tremor |
| ship | ✗ drop | Hydrophone-dominant transients during shipping passes |
| whale | ✗ drop | Fin/blue whale calls (15-30 Hz, repeating patterns) |
| t_phase | ✗ drop | Distant teleseismic energy via SOFAR |
| volcanic_tremor | ✗ drop (Stage 6 may revisit) | Sustained harmonic near Orca submarine volcano |
| active_source | ✗ drop | Wei's airgun shots (future); known shot times mask |
[!note] Cryoseismology context
Antarctic Peninsula has substantial cryoseismic literature (e.g. Olinger, Aster). Cataloging icequakes feeds into ice-loss / mass-balance / glacial-dynamics studies separate from the tectonic question. Keep the methodology open enough that the icequake catalog can be analyzed independently.
Pick CSV stream from [[01-ml-picking]] ( catalogs/picks/<NET>.<STA>/*.csv ).
Continuous waveforms (already on disk; need 3C seismic + hydrophone).
Optional: shot log from BRAVOSEIS / Wei active source for hard masking.
Manual ground truth from [[manual_picks]] for the tectonic class.
These are the signal-domain features for the classifier; ranked roughly by usefulness for our OBS-heavy network.
Onset gradient — sharp impulsive (EQ) vs gradual emergent (icequake). Easy to compute as the slope of the STA envelope around the pick.
Spectral centroid + bandwidth — calving and basal stick-slip usually more narrow-band and lower-centroid than local tectonic EQs.
Coda Q-factor (decay rate) — ice is highly scattering + absorptive → long, slowly-decaying codas. Earthquakes decay fast.
Harmonic content — glacial tremor shows parallel bands in the spectrogram (regular harmonic stripes). So does Orca volcanic tremor — needs location to separate.
Duration / magnitude scaling — icequakes are longer for their amplitude than EQs (multi-subevent source processes).
The OBS hydrophone ( ?DH ) is the single most useful channel for cryo-vs-tectonic.
Hydrophone:seismometer amplitude ratio — Tectonic local: H ≈ Z (slightly weaker on H).
Submerged cryo (calving, iceberg break-up): H equal to or stronger than Z (acoustic coupling into water column).
T-phase / ship / whale: H dominates by 10× or more.
P-onset coherence — tectonic: P on H aligns to ~1 sample with Z. T-phase / whale / continuous noise: no coherent P.
Bubble pulses / repeating coda on H — strong tell for iceberg disintegration / calving events.
S-P time — very short (<2 s) for surface-source cryo at ice margins.
Apparent depth — cryo locates near 0 km; Bransfield tectonic at 5-25 km. Becomes the cleanest discriminator once [[04-location]] runs, but it's a feedback, not an input feature.
Engineered features (~10 per pick): centroid, bandwidth, coda Q, H:Z ratio, P-onset coherence, onset slope, harmonic-stripe energy, S-P time, duration. Interpretable; feeds a gradient-boosted-tree classifier.
Spectrogram CNN in parallel: 2-D spectrogram window around each pick → CNN → class. Transfer-learn from published Antarctic cryo classifiers (PNSN cryo, Olinger/Aster work) rather than from scratch.
Vote between the two. Disagreement → flag for manual review + add to training-set queue. Keeps the loop going.
Shot-time masking (deterministic) — exclude picks within ±N s of known shot times.
Per-pick spectral / polarization features — used both for rule-based classes and as ML inputs: Dominant frequency, bandwidth, spectral centroid (T-phases vs EQs vs whales)
Rectilinearity / planarity (P-wave linearity)
Hydrophone-to-seismometer ratio (T-phase, ship, whale tells)
Duration / coda shape (icequakes are typically emergent + long-coda)
Time-of-day / inter-event interval (whale calls cluster; ships are continuous)
ML classifier on a short window around each pick — start with a published architecture (DiTing-style or simple CNN on spectrograms); train on labeled examples.
Post-association sanity — events that don't locate plausibly with [[03-association]] flag for re-classification.
[!note] Order matters — cheap-first cascade
Shot mask → spectral rules → ML → post-association sanity. Cheap filters first reduce ML inference cost.
Tectonic positives: manual picks from [[manual_picks]] (58k+).
Icequake positives: need labeled examples. Options: Hand-label a few hundred from the BRAVOSEIS waveforms (look for emergent onsets near the ice shelf).
Use any existing cryo-event catalogs from BRAVOSEIS or other Antarctic projects.
Bootstrap: train on tectonic-only first, then iterate on rejected picks to find icequake clusters.
Ship/whale/T-phase negatives: can often be auto-labeled with rules (high hydrophone:seismometer ratio + spectral signature) before any ML.
catalogs/picks_classified.csv — every Stage 1 pick with: class , class_prob , feature_* columns.
catalogs/picks_tectonic.csv — filtered to class == "tectonic" , schema-compatible with [[03-association]].
catalogs/picks_icequake.csv — filtered to class == "icequake" , schema as above for an icequake-specific Stage 3 run.
Stage 2 also closes a gap in [[manual_picks]] validation: once classification is in place, FP attribution from scripts/05_validate_picks.py can be split into
FP_tectonic — PhaseNet pick, classed as tectonic, no manual match. Real model error.
FP_icequake — PhaseNet pick, classed as icequake. Expected; counts toward icequake catalog instead.
FP_other — non-seismic noise. Drop silently.
This is the headline precision metric for Stage 1 sign-off. Until Stage 2 exists, use --event-window mode in the validator to avoid penalizing PhaseNet for finding icequakes/whales/ships.
Distant calving loses high-frequency content; spectrum starts to look like a distant tectonic EQ. Need location (depth → 0 km vs 5-25 km) to break the tie.
Orca volcanic tremor and glacial tremor are nearly identical in spectrum — both harmonic narrow-band. Separation is by location (Orca at -62.45° lat -58.45° lon vs ice margins at the basin's north/south coasts), not signal alone.
Boundary events (hybrid cryo-tectonic, slow-slip, ice-quake-triggered earthquakes) will exist; the classifier will return mass on both classes. Treat as a separate "uncertain" bin and human-review.

Locked stack:
PyOcto (Stage 3 association, coarse hypocenters)
 ↓
NLLoc — absolute locations ← user has this set up already with Orca 3D + 1D

Waveform cross-correlation differential times (sub-sample)

GrowClust — relative relocation, tight clusters

Run the full stack twice : once for the tectonic class from [[02-discrimination]], once for the icequake class. Different velocity priors, different depth priors, separate output catalogs.
Sparse + azimuthally biased network demands probabilistic absolute locations (NLLoc oct-tree gives PDFs, not point estimates).
Deep OBS (1019–1943 m water) require explicit water-layer travel-time corrections — already in catalogs/station_geometry.csv .
ML pick outliers on OBS make GrowClust the safer first-pass DD method (median-based, robust to bad CC pairs) over HypoDD (LSQR sensitive to outliers).
Dense rift cluster + Orca volcano benefit from the user's existing 3D blended velocity model in NLLoc.
Two seismicity classes in one dataset require class-aware depth priors: cryo near 0 km, tectonic at 5–25 km.
[!important] User has the NLLoc setup written
Existing config + 3D velocity model + 1D background. Bring it in at Stage 4 — do not rewrite from scratch. Confirm format and station-file compatibility with our catalogs/station_geometry.csv before running.
To clarify when we get there:
3D velocity model file format (and converter, if needed, for NLLoc grid format).
Coordinate system / projection / origin lat/lon of the 3D grid.
Vp/Vs assumption — model is Vp-only; need a Vp/Vs ratio to generate S travel-times. Typical for our crustal context: ~1.78. Verify against any published Bransfield S-wave studies.
1D background model file (user will provide; lives in data/velocity_models/ ).
Station file: convert catalogs/station_geometry.csv → NLLoc station list (lat, lon, elev — using our water_depth_m to get the seafloor sensor elevations correctly).
Depth prior — class-aware: tectonic 5–25 km, icequake 0–2 km. Encoded in NLLoc with LOCSEARCH OCT constraints + LOCMETH priors.
This step sits between NLLoc and GrowClust. It produces sub-sample-precision differential times from waveform similarity — and is the single biggest accuracy lever in the whole pipeline.
For each event pair within ~5 km of each other, cut a window around each P (and S) arrival, cross-correlate, take the lag at peak coherence.
Tools: lassie , EQcorrscan , or a custom ObsPy-based loop. EQcorrscan is the most popular for spreading-axis catalogs.
Output: catalogs/dt_cc.txt — GrowClust- and HypoDD-compatible format.
[!note] Worth as much engineering as the locator
Catalog-only DD (NLLoc-pick-time differences) gives ~100 m relative precision. CC-DD gets to ~10 m. Don't skip the CC step.
Inputs: NLLoc absolute hypocenters + dt_cc.txt + station file + 1D model (or 3D extracted to a 1D-per-station table).
Hierarchical cluster tree, median-robust, native QC flags per event.
Output: catalogs/events_growclust.csv with new lat/lon/depth + cluster IDs + quality flags.
Same DD math as HypoDD but with 3D ray tracing. Use the same Orca 3D + 1D blended model as NLLoc.
Run on a curated high-quality subset (well-recorded, low-residual events from 4a).
Compare GrowClust vs tomoDD locations on the same events. Agreement → publishable.

These are now in [[01-ml-picking]] but worth surfacing here as the day's "discoveries":
ZX OBS use low-gain seismometer code ( ?L? ), not high-gain ( ?H? ). Initial channel filter EH?,HH?,BH?,SH? returned zero for ZX. Real channels: ELZ @ 200 Hz vertical, SL1 / SL2 @ 100 Hz horizontals, EDH @ 200 Hz hydrophone.
ZX is a reused temp network code spanning 2003–2022 across multiple deployments (Bransfield 2019, New Zealand 2021/2022, China, UK, Costa Rica). Filter to BRA* station glob + 2019-01 → 2020-03 window.
5M is also reused — bbox filter to Bransfield, since the same code includes European stations.
R4DE2 epoch trap — the same Raspberry Shake station code has bounced between Uruguay and Bransfield several times. FDSN bbox filter at the channel-epoch level (Raspberry Shake supports it) drops the Uruguay epochs cleanly. Within our window, only ~5 days of true Bransfield data; after 2020-08 it's continuous through 2025 if we ever extend the window.
OBS water depth comes free from StationXML — elevation field is negative for seafloor sensors. GEBCO not needed for Stage 1; only for 3D ray paths in Stage 4.
Mixed sample rates within a single ZX station (200 Hz vertical, 100 Hz horizontals). Picker resamples Z to 100 Hz before PhaseNet.
Three files dropped in data/manual_picks/ : two NLLoc obs ( nllmaleen_*.out ) + one Nordic / SeisAn ( collect_regional.out ).
Parsed to canonical schema → catalogs/manual_picks.csv . 58,630 picks across 6,970 events.
Two parser quirks captured: Nordic packs station+component without whitespace (need fixed-column slicing); magnitude regex needs the last match per line, bounded to plausible range.
One mystery flagged: BRA05 appears in manual picks (239 times) but not in our FDSN-resolved inventory.
User pointed out that BRA05 is on GEOFON, not EarthScope. Cross-checking revealed 8 additional BRAVOSEIS OBS stations hosted at GEOFON: BRA02, 03, 04, 05, 08, 09, 10, 11. Total deployment = 22 OBS, with no overlap between the two data centers. Missing: BRA01, 06, 07, 12, 17 (assumed failed deployments).
The GEOFON-hosted OBS use a different instrument type — high-gain broadband at uniform 100 Hz ( HHZ/HH1/HH2 ), vs. the EarthScope-hosted low-gain mixed-rate stations. Both work with PhaseNet (resampled to 100 Hz) but downstream discrimination/location may need to treat them separately.
Inventory bumped: 560 GB total / 1.4 TB recommended free disk (was 435 GB / 1.1 TB).
Config now has two ZX targets (one per data center). Fixed a bug where both targets wrote to the same ZX_BRAALL.xml — now suffixed with data center.
Built the missing pieces so PhaseNet output can be measured against manual ground truth as soon as it exists:
manual_picks.resolve_networks() joins picks against station_geometry.csv to fill in network codes (NLLoc/Nordic don't carry them). 58,606 / 58,630 picks resolved; only ESPZ + OHG (24 picks, Antarctic regional stations outside our targets) stay blank.
scripts/05_validate_picks.py — greedy nearest-time matcher. For each (network, station, phase) reports TP/FP/FN, precision, recall, F1, residual mean/std. Defaults: P ±0.5 s, S ±1.0 s. Writes catalogs/validation_report.csv (per net × sta × phase) and catalogs/validation_per_pick.csv (per-pick, including residuals). Handles empty PhaseNet directory.
User flagged that icequakes are a research target , not just noise. Reshaped Stage 2 from binary "filter to tectonic" to multi-class classification :
Keep + catalog: tectonic, icequake (two parallel output catalogs)
Drop: ships, whales, T-phases, volcanic tremor (Orca), active-source shots
Output structure: picks_classified.csv (every pick with class + features), picks_tectonic.csv and picks_icequake.csv (split outputs that feed parallel Stage 3 association runs).
Implication: hydrophone download (already enabled) is now load-bearing — needed for ship/whale/T-phase discrimination and for cryoseismic feature extraction. Also needs labeled icequake examples for training.
This also closes the validation loop properly: once Stage 2 exists, Stage 1 FP attribution splits into FP_tectonic (real model error), FP_icequake (counts toward icequake catalog), and FP_other (silent drop).

Discussed associators and locators in detail:
Associator: PyOcto (Münchmeyer, same author as SeisBench). SeisBench itself doesn't include an associator; PyOcto is the natural pairing — fast octree search, robust to ML pick noise, drops in directly. GaMMA reserved for a 1-week sanity cross-check.
Locator stack: PyOcto → NLLoc → waveform CC → GrowClust → tomoDD (optional) . NLLoc gives PDFs (essential for our sparse, azimuthally biased network). GrowClust chosen over HypoDD as primary DD because median-based solver is more robust to ML pick outliers. tomoDD on a curated subset for cross-validation.
Velocity model: user has an Orca 3D blended with a 1D background, and an existing NLLoc setup using it. Bring it in at Stage 4 — do not rewrite. Vp only; will use Vp/Vs ≈ 1.78 for S travel-times. User will provide the 1D background model file.
Run the full Stage 3-4 stack twice — once for tectonic, once for icequake — with different velocity priors and depth ranges.
Cross-correlation step between NLLoc and GrowClust is the biggest precision lever (catalog-only DD: ~100 m, CC-DD: ~10 m). Use EQcorrscan or similar.
Stage 3 + 4 vault notes updated with the locked stack.

Ran the full Stage 1 workflow on one day to validate before cluster commitment.
Download ( 02_download_waveforms.py --start 2019-12-26 --end 2019-12-27 ):
35 / 37 stations returned data (R4DE2 correctly excluded — Uruguay epoch on this date).
1.66 GB total (~2× initial estimate; reasonable with hydrophone + GEOFON OBS included).
Picking ( 03_run_phasenet.py ):
CPU on M-series Mac, 17 min for 35 station-days.
Peak RAM 3.1 GB (PhaseNet activations + ObsPy stream).
Wall time scales linearly: full year × 38 stations ≈ 135 hours sequential, ~17 hours with an 8-way SLURM array, ~2 hours with GPU.
Validation against manual picks (Dec 26 has 23 unique manual picks across 2 events; required dedup since mag07 ⊂ magall was double-counting):
| Setting | Stations w/ picks | ML picks | P recall | S recall | P prec (event-window) | S prec (event-window) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stead @ 0.3 | 32 | 2,068 | 9% (1/11) | 17% (2/12) | 33% | 33% |
| instance
 @ 0.2 | 35 | 3,307 | 45% (5/11) | 42% (5/12) | 38% | 63% |
Both recall AND precision up — the rare double win. Default switched in 03_run_phasenet.py and slurm/pick.sbatch to instance weights @ threshold 0.2. STEAD is land-only training data; instance was trained on European OBS, much closer to BRAVOSEIS domain.
Why recall isn't higher yet: PhaseNet still picks events on a different subset of stations than the manual analyst — for the 13:43:42 event, manual used BRA14/16/19/20/21/22/25 and PhaseNet used BRA05/13/14/15/16/18. Only BRA14 + BRA16 overlap. Doesn't matter for association (PyOcto only needs ≥4 stations), but limits per-station validation. Future fine-tuning on Bransfield manual picks should close more of the gap.

sectionTitle: PhaseNet caught a missed event at 23:51:34 — validation win
sectionPath: PhaseNet caught a missed event at 23:51:34 — validation win
text:
While inspecting Dec 26 results, a 4-station cluster surfaced at 23:51:34–36 , ~24 s after manual event 2 (23:51:10). PhaseNet picks at BRA19/BRA21/BRA22/BRA20 with S-P times of 0.6–0.8 s on the cleanest stations — a real, second local seismic event the manual analyst either missed or merged with event 2 . Not coda of event 2 (24 s gap is far too long for a local source).
[!warning] Don't call this an "aftershock" yet
Earlier draft labeled this as an aftershock — that overclaimed. We don't have magnitudes or locations yet, so the physical relationship between the two events is unconstrained. Better-supported labels for a Bransfield rift+volcanic context: Earthquake swarm pair (most likely; characteristic of spreading axes and volcanic regions)
Doublet/multiplet on the same fault patch
Triggered seismicity (static or dynamic stress transfer)
Aftershock if event 1 turns out to be larger
Foreshock–mainshock if event 2 is larger Pinning it down needs Stage 4 magnitudes + locations + waveform CC between the two.
Notes:
Borderline confidence under instance weights (BRA19 P prob 0.34 vs 0.97 with stead ). Suggests an ensemble may help on marginal events.
4 stations is right at PyOcto's typical association minimum — won't be lost downstream.
This is exactly the upside of running an ML picker over the full record: catalog-completeness gain, not just QA against the existing catalog.
Captured in [[01-ml-picking]] under "PhaseNet caught a missed event at +25 s".
Re-ran Dec 26 picks with instance @ 0.1 (down from 0.2):
| Setting | ML picks | P recall | S recall | P prec (EW) | S prec (EW) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| stead @ 0.3 | 2,068 | 9% | 17% | 33% | 33% |
| instance @ 0.2 | 3,307 | 45% | 42% | 38% | 63% |
| instance
 @ 0.1 | 6,902 | 64% | 42% | 47% | 63% |
P recall jumped 45 → 64 % with precision also up (rare double win). S recall flat — bounded by something other than threshold (likely OBS horizontals being noisier on small events). instance @ 0.1
 locked as the new default. Defaults updated in 03_run_phasenet.py and slurm/pick.sbatch .
Ran EQT @ instance @ 0.1 on Dec 26 (same data, separate output dir catalogs/picks_eqt_instance/ ):
| Model | Total picks | P | S | P recall | S recall | P prec (EW) | S prec (EW) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PhaseNet | 6,902 | 5,809 | 1,093 | 64% | 42% | 47% | 63% |
| EQTransformer | 7,126 | 5,939 | 1,187 | 36% | 50% | 31% | 67% |
Mixed result, complementary strengths:
PhaseNet wins on P (U-Net excels at sharp impulsive arrivals).
EQT wins on S (transformer + LSTM better for variable-character S onsets).
Recommendation: run both on the cluster (cheap on GPU); union of picks → PyOcto handles overlap during association. Coded --model and --out-subdir flags in 03_run_phasenet.py to support side-by-side runs.
Read [[srl-2024086.1.pdf]] (Wang, Waldhauser, Schaff, Tolstoy, Wilcock, Tan — "Real-Time Detection of Volcanic Unrest and Eruption at Axial Seamount Using Machine Learning"). Their stack:
PhaseNet → GaMMA → NLLoc → HypoDD + waveform CC → SpecUFEx (unsupervised classification)
+ 30-50/4-50 Hz freq-ratio rule for fin-whale calls
+ 15s overlapping windows in real-time (6s during high seismicity)
Validates our locked stack almost component-for-component. Things to adopt:
SpecUFEx unsupervised feature clustering for [[02-discrimination]] — alternative or complement to our planned supervised CNN.
Whale-call frequency ratio rule (30–50 / 4–50 Hz energy) — drop-in deterministic discriminator.
1 s pre-P + 3 s post-P spectrogram window for classification features — adopt as default.
PhaseNet pick std on OBS : 17 ms (P), 40/28 ms (S) — useful prior for our CC differential-time uncertainty.
Self-training (Yarowsky) for label reconciliation across stations — useful pattern for class-aware FP attribution.
What we do that they don't: explicit hydrophone features, manual analyst picks as direct ground truth. Their training data was Kurtosis-picked baseline.
User has a free 32-CPU 128-GB cluster, with options including a Pytorch instance (32 CPU + 187 GB + 1 GPU) . Decision: use Pytorch from the start since GPUs are free. Single-instance workflow:
Setup: 5 min
Verify on 1 day with --device cuda : ~5 min
Full year download: ~2-3 h (FDSN-bound, GPU idle)
Full year picking on GPU: ~30-60 min (vs 17 h on 32 CPUs)
Validation: <1 min
If both PhaseNet + EQT runs are wanted: ~2 h total picking on GPU.
Quick poor-man's associator (≥4 stations within 5s window) on PhaseNet picks for Dec 26 finds ~214 candidate event clusters . Manual catalog has only 2 events. Hourly distribution of clusters is roughly uniform — doesn't suggest dominant ship/whale (diurnal) noise contamination.
Realistic estimate after proper PyOcto association (spatial+temporal coherence): ~50-100 events , of which maybe 30-60 tectonic and 20-40 cryo after Stage 2. 15-30× catalog completeness gain vs the manual catalog for this single day.
Implication: the manual catalog is a hand-curated subset (probably triggered-detector + magnitude/quality cutoff), not a complete record. Use it as a validation set for ML accuracy on confirmed events, not as ground truth for completeness — i.e., don't treat "missing from manual" as evidence of false positive.
scripts/plot_manual_picks_day.py produces per-event waveform plots:
Solid lines = manual picks, dashed = PhaseNet, dotted = EQT ( --ml-subdirs picks,picks_eqt_instance )
Stations on each panel = union of stations with any pick (manual OR ML) within ±2 s of event window — not just analyst-picked stations
--center-time mode for plotting events with no manual entry (e.g., the 23:51:34 second event)
Output: figures/picks_<date>_<event-id>.png
Three figures generated for Dec 26 (events 1, 2, second event at +24 s) — visually confirms ML pickers track manual picks tightly when both fire, and EQT recovers some S that PhaseNet misses.
In rough priority order:
~~Investigate BRA05 ~~ — resolved (GEOFON-hosted).
~~Threshold tuning~~ — instance @ 0.1 locked.
~~Compare PhaseNet vs EQT~~ — both have strengths; run both on cluster.
Verify on cluster — Pytorch GPU instance, run 1 day end-to-end, confirm numbers match laptop.
Full-year cluster run — download (~2-3 h) + PhaseNet + EQT picking on GPU (~2 h total) + validate.
Add PyOcto association to the pipeline so we have real event counts, not pick counts.
Begin Stage 2 (multi-class classification: tectonic + icequake) — adopt SpecUFEx unsupervised clustering + whale freq-ratio rule from Wang 2024.
Pin down the 23:51:34 second event physically — magnitudes, locations, waveform CC against event 2 — once Stage 4 lands.

noteTitle: Plan — OBS noise denoiser + PhaseNet fine-tuning
sectionPath: Plan — OBS noise denoiser + PhaseNet fine-tuning
text:
The 14-month BRAVOSEIS deployment is all the data we have. The goal is an expanded earthquake catalog beyond what the manual analyst caught ( nllmaleen_mag07_202210.out — 12,099 picks across 1,126 events). The baseline picker (PhaseNet instance + OBSTransformer @ 0.5) recovered only P recall ≈ 0.42 / S recall ≈ 0.78 on Feb 4–13 — too many easy events are slipping through. The fix is two-sided: Train a DeepDenoiser on BRAVOSEIS-OBS waveforms — an STFT U-Net seisbench.models.DeepDenoiser , initialised from original weights and adapted to OBS noise. Fine-tune PhaseNet on a curated set of 30 high-density days, using the trained denoiser to (a) generate noise-mixed training variants and (b) optionally provide a "cleaned" event channel. Honest evaluation on a fully-held-out August 2019 (1,144 picks over 26 active days, 106 events). This plan refines the existing draft to align with the repo's actual conventions ( catalogs/picks// , catalogs/manual_picks.csv , --out-subdir , the existing match_one_group matcher in scripts/05_validate_picks.py ) and removes references to files that the draft assumed existed but don't ( scripts/06_* , scripts/07_* , phasenet-retrain clone). flowchart TB subgraph inputs[Inputs] WAV[data/waveforms/NET/STA/*.mseed] MAN[catalogs/manual_picks.csv

Phase 2 — 31 variants/pick] EVH --> AUG NSH --> AUG AUG --> AUGDS[(data/seisbench/bransfield_aug.h5
~100k windows)] AUGDS --> FT[09_finetune_phasenet.py
Phase 3 — Lightning fine-tune] FT --> FTCKPT[(models/phasenet_bransfield_v1/best.ckpt)] FTCKPT --> RUN[03_run_phasenet.py
--weights ckpt:<path>

File: scripts/test_deepdenoiser.py (NEW, throwaway) Load sbm.DeepDenoiser.from_pretrained('original') . Pull 3 mag07 event windows + 3 noise windows directly from data/waveforms/... using mseed_path() and the pick times from catalogs/manual_picks.csv (filter source_file contains mag07 , uncertainty_s ≤ 0.1 ). Apply denoiser via model.annotate(stream) per docs, plot original/denoised/residual to figures/dd_sanity/*.png . Decision: if denoised events look mangled (impulsive arrivals lost), retraining is required (Phase 1 is mandatory). If reasonable, retraining is still the plan but we have a cheap fallback.

sectionTitle: Phase 1 — Build OBS noise/event pools, train OBS-DeepDenoiser (~1 h GPU)
sectionPath: Plan — OBS noise denoiser + PhaseNet fine-tuning
Phase 1 — Build OBS noise/event pools, train OBS-DeepDenoiser (~1 h GPU)
text:
File: scripts/06_extract_event_noise.py (NEW)
Walk the 30 curated training days (see § Training day list ) and the
station inventory:
Event windows: for each mag07 pick with uncertainty_s ≤ 0.1 on a
curated day, cut a 30 s window around the pick from the matching
 data/waveforms/<NET>/<STA>/*.mseed . Reuse _channel_match() from
 scripts/03_run_phasenet.py for picking-channel selection. Target rate
100 Hz (matches --target-rate default), 3-channel ZNE.
Noise windows: for each curated station-day, sample candidate 30 s
windows and gate them through three filters before keeping: Manual-pick exclusion — >60 s from any pick in both 
 nllmaleen_mag07_202210.out and nllmaleen_magall_202210.out 
( magall ⊃ mag07 and catches the lower-confidence events the draft's
 mag07 -only filter would have missed).
STA/LTA detector reject — run
 obspy.signal.trigger.classic_sta_lta(tr, nsta=int(0.5*fs), nlta=int(10*fs)) 
on the candidate window's vertical channel and reject if any sample
exceeds ratio 3.0. Catches events the analyst missed and non-tectonic
transients (icequakes, whales, ships, T-phases) — exactly what the
denoiser must treat as noise, not signal.
Amplitude sanity — reject windows whose RMS is <1e-3 × the
station-day median RMS (dropouts/dead channels) or >10 × median
(clipping/spikes that aren't real noise).
Target ~500 surviving windows per curated station-day. Plot the
acceptance rate per station-day to figures/noise_qc.png so we can spot
stations with pathological selection (e.g. 5 % acceptance → station has
swarm activity outside mag07 catalog).
Write SeisBench-format datasets: data/seisbench/bransfield_events.h5 + metadata.csv
data/seisbench/bransfield_noise.h5 + metadata.csv
File: scripts/07_train_obs_denoiser.py (NEW)
DeepDenoiser is a masking STFT U-Net: given (signal + noise), it predicts
a TF mask isolating the signal. SeisBench's STFTDenoiserLabeller builds
the supervisory mask from clean signal + noise pairs.
- model = sbm.DeepDenoiser.from_pretrained('original')
- generator pipeline:
 pick random event window from bransfield_events
 pick random noise window from bransfield_noise
 mix at SNR ∈ [0.5, 10]
 STFTDenoiserLabeller -> mask
- Train: AdamW, lr 1e-4, batch 32, 50 epochs, MSE on mask
- 90/10 split by station (held-out stations validate generalisation,
 not just held-out windows of the same station)
- Save best by val_loss to models/deepdenoiser_obs/best.pt
Verify: plot 6 held-out windows pre/post denoising; val_loss curve
in figures/dd_train_loss.png .
File: scripts/08_build_augmented_dataset.py (NEW)
For each of ~3,300 high-confidence picks across the 30 curated training days
(filter source_file contains mag07 AND uncertainty_s ≤ 0.1 ):
30 noise variants: mix the event window with random noise samples
from bransfield_noise.h5 at SNR ∈ [0.5, 10].
1 denoised variant: apply the OBS-DeepDenoiser checkpoint from
Phase 1.
→ ~31 × 3,300 ≈ ~100k SeisBench-format training windows in
 data/seisbench/bransfield_aug.h5 + metadata.csv . Each row carries
per-pick P/S sample indices for PhaseNet's ProbabilisticLabeller .
The dataloader in Phase 3 layers fresh online noise mixing + temporal
jitter + channel dropout on top each epoch — pre-materialising 31 variants
is for speed, online aug for variety.
File: scripts/09_finetune_phasenet.py (NEW)
We're not vendoring phasenet-retrain as separate copies — instead,
write a single self-contained Lightning script that uses SeisBench's own
training pipeline ( sbg.GenericGenerator , sbg.WaveformDataset ,
PhaseNet's built-in forward + cross-entropy on the 3-channel
target mask). This avoids importing a third-party package and patching
its _load_custom_data() NotImplementedError stub.
Skeleton:
- model = sbm.PhaseNet.from_pretrained('instance') # transfer learning
- ds = sbd.WaveformDataset('data/seisbench/bransfield_aug')
- generator = sbg.GenericGenerator(ds)
 generator.add_augmentations([
 RandomWindow(samples=3001),
 ChangeDtype(np.float32),
 Normalize(detrend_axis=-1),
 ProbabilisticLabeller(label_columns=['P','S']),
 # online aug:
 OneOf([NoiseMix(p=0.5), GaussianNoise(p=0.3), Identity(p=0.2)]),
 ChannelDropout(p=0.1),
 ])
- Lightning Trainer: max_epochs 30, batch 64, lr 1e-4, AdamW
- Save best by val P+S F1 to models/phasenet_bransfield_v1/best.ckpt
Config: configs/phasenet_finetune.yaml (NEW) — pretrained tag,
data path, hyperparameters. Keep alongside configs/targets.yaml .

scripts/build_velocity_model.py regenerates configs/velocity_model.csv from
 configs/Pg_Orca_velocity.nc :
Median Vp at each Orca depth across the 101×136 (x,y) cell volume.
Orca's z=0 is at the seafloor (top-cell median Vp=1.91 km/s blends water+sediment).
New 1D model uses sea-level datum, with a 1.3 km water layer prepended: Water: Vp = 1.4558 km/s (measured Bransfield water-column velocity per Kidiwela+ SI,
1455.8 m/s — WOA09 January mean equals XBT mean to 1.6 m/s).
Water Vs = 0.5 km/s (small positive value — physically meaningless, but pyocto's
Eikonal solver crashes on Vs=0).
Rock 1.3 → 11.3 km below sea level: Orca median Vp, Vs = Vp/1.78.
Deep extension 16.3 / 21.3 / 31.3 km: hand-picked Vp = 6.6 / 6.8 / 7.0 km/s (notes/13).
Plot: notes/figures/velocity_model.png (Orca 3D→1D averaging on left; new 1D with linear
interpolation between actual nodes on right).

notes/supporting info.pdf Table S1 gives inverted lon/lat (from joint inversion of 8394
acoustic water-wave arrivals) and bathymetric depths (from Almendros et al. 2020) for 15 OBS.
The paper recommends using inverted horizontal + bathymetric depth (the inverted z is biased by
the uniform water-velocity assumption).
scripts/apply_S1_corrections.py patches catalogs/station_geometry.csv :
All 15 ZX stations: lon/lat → inverted (median 133 m correction, max 243 m).
13 ZX stations: water_depth_m → bathymetric (most diffs <30 m; BRA25 was 430 m wrong :
was 1326 m, now 896 m).
Backup at catalogs/station_geometry.csv.bak_pre_S1 .
BRA05 clock correction : paper Text S1 reports OBS clock running fast by +0.167 s (no drift).
Script subtracts 0.167 s from time , start , end columns of every BRA05 pick CSV in both
 catalogs/picks_obst_01/ZX.BRA05/ (398 files) and /home/jovyan/my_data/bravoseis/picks/ZX.BRA05/ 
(398 files). Idempotent via .bra05_clock_corrected marker.
It isn't for ray tracing — first-arrival rays from sub-seafloor events to seafloor OBS never
traverse water. The water layer exists for vertical-datum bookkeeping : each OBS sits at a
different seafloor depth (1019 → 1499 m, ~500 m spread). With a sea-level datum pyocto needs some 
medium between z=0 (sea surface) and z=1.3 km (top of rock) where the stations live. Without it,
pyocto would treat the column above each OBS as rock, which is fiction. Water Vp value doesn't
affect arrival times (no rays go through it for our geometry); Vs was forced to 0.5 km/s only
because the Eikonal solver crashes on Vs=0.
Alternative would be a seafloor datum (z=0 = seafloor), all OBS at z=0, accepting the ~500 m
inter-station spread as ~0.1–0.3 s pick noise. We chose the sea-level / water-layer route to keep
each station at its actual measured depth.
5M.* land stations on the South Shetland islands have elevations 0 → +30 m in the inventory. With
sea-level datum, pyocto would place them at z = -elevation/1000 km, i.e., slightly above the model
top (z=0). Pyocto clamps z<0 to the top layer for ray tracing, so effectively all land stations
are treated as sitting at sea level. The error: at most 30 m vertical = ≤0.01 s travel-time bias
at crustal Vp, well below pick_tol=0.5 s. Land stations are ≥30 km from Bransfield rift events
anyway, so ray paths are long and the vertical offset rounds out. Left as-is.

sectionTitle: Pyocto: from 16h monolithic failure → daily chunks in parallel
sectionPath: Pyocto: from 16h monolithic failure → daily chunks in parallel
text:
Failed approach (replicated from yesterday's stuck run): single associate() call on the whole year, 8 threads, hit 16h with zero output written. Was killed.
Working approach : daily chunks running in parallel ( scripts/17e_pyocto_daily_year.sh ):
1 chunk per day, 10 threads each, 10 chunks at a time (100 cores per batch)
425 days total → 43 batches of 10 days each
Each batch runs in parallel; next batch only starts when current finishes
Resume-capable: skips any day already in catalogs/pyocto_daily/events_YYYY-MM-DD.csv
Per-day output written immediately on completion — full visibility, no all-or-nothing risk
Per-day timing (post-OBS-online, n≥5 stations):
Quiet day: 5–10 min
Dense swarm day (e.g., 2019-01-23 with 1900+ events): 30–45 min
Whole-year extrapolation: ~22h wall
Boundary safety : each chunk loads picks from [day_start − 120s, day_end + 120s] ( --margin-seconds 120 ) so events near midnight see their late-arriving picks. After associate() , events whose origin time falls outside the strict day are filtered out so the adjacent chunks don't double-count them. Confirmed working via Jan 9 chunk's log:
strict window: [2019-01-09 00:00, 2019-01-10 00:00)
load window: [2019-01-08 23:58, 2019-01-10 00:02) (+120s margin)
margin filter: kept 9/9 events in strict window
Filename pre-filter optimization : the original load_picks_for_pyocto() scanned all 28,000 year-long CSVs for every chunk and filtered by timestamp. Now it only opens CSVs whose filename's day-of-year falls inside the load window — ~76 files per chunk instead of 28,000. Brought per-day startup from ~10 min to <10s.

scripts/17_pyocto_associate.py :
Missing 
id
 column on stations — pyocto ≥0.6 requires id on the stations DataFrame in addition to the station / network columns. Added stations["id"] = stations["station"] before associator.associate(...) .
Missing 
transform_stations()
 call — pyocto needs local x/y/z columns projected via the associator's CRS, set by associator.transform_stations(stations) . Old script omitted this and failed with Columns 'x', 'y', 'z' expected ... .
Pick
 constructor expects float epoch seconds, not pd.Timestamp — newer pyocto C++ binding signature is Pick(int, float, str, str) . Was passing picks_in["time"] as datetime which fails. Fix: picks_in["time"] = picks_in["time"].astype("int64") / 1e9 .
Eikonal solver 
EikonalExtError: unexpected/untested code executed — caused by Vs = 0 in the water layer (pyrocko's solver divides by Vs). Set water Vs = 0.5 km/s (physically meaningless but safe — rays from sub-seafloor sources never traverse water, so Fermat routes them through faster rock anyway).
--label
 choice restricted — original script's argparse choices=["picker_only", "with_manual"] rejected arbitrary chunk labels like monthly_2019-01 . Loosened to free-form, still triggers with_manual behaviour only on that exact label.
Also added:
Timestamped progress logging via _log() helper + python -u for unbuffered output
Per-phase wall-time tracking (pick load / model build / associator / associate)
Exception printing with full traceback before exit
Pre-flight stats: per-station pick counts, station z range, pick time-range sanity checks

Started in parallel with pyocto's daily run on 30 days of partial catalog ( catalogs/pyocto_events_partial30days.csv , 11,358 events, 154,168 picks). Two more bugs found here before it would run correctly:
pd.to_datetime
 without 
unit='s' — pyocto saves time as float epoch-seconds. pd.to_datetime(float, utc=True) defaults to interpreting numeric input as nanoseconds → every event ended up on 1970-01-01. Waveform path lookup then targets *.1970.001.mseed which doesn't exist → kept 0 pairs / 0 obs for ~10 min before we caught it. Fix: detect numeric dtype and force unit="s" .
ProcessPoolExecutor
 imported but never used — --workers 24 arg was a no-op; the cross-correlation loop ran single-threaded. Rewrote the loop with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) over _process_anchor(anchor) workers. Threads are fine here because the work is I/O-bound (mseed reads) + numpy XC (releases GIL).
These two were silent-correctness failures — script printed normal progress lines while producing useless output. Updated the monitor's grep filter to flag kept 0 pairs and events: 0 patterns so similar bugs don't waste time again.
Status of XC prep launch: 309,641 unique event pairs identified within 5 km, 24-thread cross-correlation running, ~3-4 cores effectively busy (I/O dominated). RSS 16 GB (waveform caches per anchor).
Best-RMS event (idx 148 on 2019-01-28, RMS=0.117 s, 16 stations, depth 0.6 km below sea level): waveform stack at notes/figures/pyocto_event_2019-01-28_idx148_waveforms.png . Impulsive P arrivals with tight moveout across all stations, S separations visible. Real local-event signature, not a false association.
Best by station count (idx 151 on 2019-01-17, RMS=0.20 s, 19 stations): waveforms at notes/figures/pyocto_event_2019-01-17_waveforms.png .

Min 0.00 s (trivial low-pick events)
P10 0.171 s

P90 0.283 s
Max 3.46 s
Pyocto's location grid is min_node_size_location = 1.5 km — events quantized at 1.5 km horizontal and ~1.25 km vertical grid centers. Final precision will come from Stage 4 (GrowClust) which refines relative positions sub-100 m using XC differential times.
1-day Jan 17 test reproduced in daily-chunk runner : 395 events (within 10 of the standalone 1-day test's 385), confirming the per-day script is equivalent.
For 2019-01-17 mag07 catalog (118 manual events):
55% pyocto-event recall within 5 s of manual origin

Ran GrowClust on the 30-day partial XC output. Five bugs uncovered in the runner
( scripts/19_run_growclust.py ) before completion:
Control file passed via stdin instead of argv[1] — GrowClust's growclust.f90:182 
reads call getarg(1, infile_ctl) , so it expects the control file as a command-line
argument. Fixed: subprocess.run([args.binary, ctl_path.name], cwd=run_dir, ...) .
Station list format incompatible — NW.STNAME (period at column 3) fell into
GrowClust's STNAME-only branch which truncates at 5 chars, then tried to parse the
remaining char as a real number ("Bad real number in item 1 of list input"). Fix:
strip network prefix from both stlist.txt and dt.cc so station codes are bare
(e.g., BRA15 , not ZX.BRA15 ).
Travel-time table distance too small — tt_del1=150 km but the network aperture
is ~165 km (5M.TOW to far events). Bumped tt_del1 to 300 km and delmax to 250 km.
Travel-time table depth too shallow — events at ≤40 km with tt_dep1=30 km .
Bumped tt_dep1 to 60 km (matches pyocto's z_max+headroom). Also extended
 configs/velocity_model.csv with a half-space marker at 70 km so the vzmodel covers
the table range.
Earlier 
dt.cc
 bug surfaced via inputs — the differential times were raw
pick-time differences (median |dt| = 21 hours instead of sub-second). Fixed in
 scripts/18b_fix_dtcc.py (post-processes existing dt.cc) and in
 scripts/18_growclust_xc_prep.py:collect_pair_dts (subtracts origin-time difference)
for future runs.
After fixes, Stage 4 wall time is negligible (<1 s for the relocation itself; the
travel-time table build dominates at ~30 s). Output: catalogs/growclust_partial30days.csv .
Quality of 30-day partial relocation:
11,358 events total; 5,037 (44%) relocated in multi-event clusters
6,321 singletons (no nearby pair partners yet — will pair up in full-year run)
530-event main cluster centered on Orca
Median displacement from pyocto: 1.57 km horizontal, 0.70 km depth — exactly the
pyocto octree grid quantization (1.5 km cells) being un-locked. Intra-cluster relative
positions are now sub-100 m.
Two upstream bugs in scripts/18_growclust_xc_prep.py cost ~2 hours each before being
found:
pd.to_datetime
 without 
unit='s' — pyocto saves time as float epoch-seconds;
 pd.to_datetime(numeric, utc=True) defaults to ns, so every event ended up on
1970-01-01. Waveform path lookup then targeted nonexistent *.1970.001.mseed files
→ cache empty → kept 0 pairs / 0 obs for 10+ minutes before we noticed. Fix: detect
numeric dtype and force unit="s" .
ProcessPoolExecutor
 imported but never used — --workers 24 was a no-op; the
cross-correlation loop ran single-threaded. Wrapped the loop in
 ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.workers) over _process_anchor(anchor) workers.
Threads (not processes) are fine because the work is I/O-bound (mseed reads) +
numpy XC which releases the GIL.
Additional efficiency rewrite: preload every station-day mseed file once into
numpy arrays at 100 Hz ( preload_all_station_days ), so the inner XC loop is pure
numpy slicing instead of repeated obspy.read() . Initial run before this rewrite
was projecting ~4 days at 24 threads; after rewrite, 67 min total wall time
(20 min preload + 47 min XC) for the 30-day partial with 309k unique event pairs.
Added patterns to catch the silent-correctness failure modes seen today:
 kept 0 pairs|events: 0|0 events|FAILED|batch N done . The original monitor only
matched explicit error tracebacks, which let the 1970-date bug churn quietly for
10 min before we saw it.
Behavioural bugs (e.g., the unused ProcessPoolExecutor with no log signature) still
require active CPU/thread inspection — no grep filter can catch them.
Pyocto daily runner ~9% through (40/425 days, ETA ~22h)
GrowClust XC prep ~15% through (24-thread, expect 1-2h on 30-day catalog; final run on full year will be ~10× this)
Stage 4 (GrowClust binary): unstarted; will launch once XC prep produces growclust/partial30days/dt.cc
TODO: add rms_residual_s derived column to merged events file before plotting / handoff
TODO: re-evaluate water-layer Vs once Stage 4 results come back (current Vs=0.5 only used by S-wave Eikonal solver outside the actual ray paths, but worth checking sensitivity)

Stage: Pyocto (Stage 2)
Method: octree centroid Horizontal: ~1.5 km grid
Vertical: ~1.25 km grid
Origin time: ~0.5 s ────────────────────────────────────────
Stage: GrowClust (Stage 4)
Method: differential XC relocation
Horizontal: <100 m (relative)
Vertical: <100 m (relative)
Origin time: sub-ms (relative)
It doesn't relocate events one by one using absolute travel times. Instead it uses the differential times between pairs of events at the same station (the dt.cc file Stage 3 isproducing). The key insight:
Absolute travel-time error from a wrong velocity model affects both events in a pair the same way at a given station
That error cancels when you difference: dt(event_A) − dt(event_B)
What's left is the genuine spatial offset between A and B, measurable to sub-millisecond via waveform cross-correlation
So GrowClust gives you:
Relative positions between events: 10–100 m precision (the real number for cluster structure)
Absolute positions: still anchored to pyocto's starting locations + the 1D velocity model. So if Orca's centroid is biased by 500 m in absolute lat/lon, the whole relocated cluster shifts by 500 m, but the internal structure is tight.
For your use case (mapping the magmatic plumbing under Orca), the relative geometry is what matters: which events lie along the same fault, what's the dyke trajectory, etc. The gridded "lines of points" you noticed in pyocto's output will disappear completely — the cluster will fan out into its true geometry.
If you also want absolute precision (e.g., to compare with the 3D tomography model), NLLoc with the Orca 3D model is the standard add-on, run independently from GrowClust.
If it crashes and we pick this up in a new session, paste me these so I can resume cold:

restart.

noteTitle: Pyocto year finished, XC prep killed by pod OOM
sectionPath: Pyocto year finished, XC prep killed by pod OOM
text:
Daily-chunk pyocto year run launched the prior session via 20_pipeline_finale.sh , which polls for the merged catalog and then auto-triggers Stage 3 (XC prep) and Stage 4 (GrowClust).
Full-year pyocto catalog: catalogs/pyocto_events_picker_only.csv — 42,040 events, 483,516 picks .
Stage 3 ( scripts/18_growclust_xc_prep.py ) reached the waveform preload phase and started reading the 12,769 referenced station-day mseed files into _WF_CACHE .
20_pipeline_finale.sh was launched twice; both runs died mid-preload:
| Run | Started (UTC) | Died (UTC) | Preload progress |
|-----|---------------|------------|------------------|
| 1 | 2026-05-12 20:31 | 2026-05-13 05:51 | 4,400 / 12,769 (~34%) |
| 2 | 2026-05-13 06:16 | 2026-05-13 ~06:34 | 4,200 / 12,769 (~33%) |
Symptom on the JupyterHub side: "Server unavailable or unreachable. Your server at /user/seismic@uw.edu/ is not running. Would you like to restart it?" — i.e. the entire pod went away, not just the terminal.
logs/pipeline_finale.log ends mid-progress with no traceback.
No python process alive afterward; dmesg clean.
/sys/fs/cgroup/memory.max = 200,789,721,088 (~187 GiB) — that's the pod's cgroup cap. The node reports 1.5 TiB in free -h , but per-user pods get far less.
memory.events.oom_kill reads 0 — that counter resets when the pod restarts, so it doesn't help post-mortem.
_WF_CACHE holds every station-day waveform in RAM for the full run. Linear extrapolation from 33% loaded → ~150-200 GiB at completion, which lands at or over the 187 GiB cap. Cgroup OOM kills the pod cleanly (no dmesg entry on the host kernel log).
nohup / setsid would not have helped: the pod itself is the unit that dies.
Eager whole-cache preload exceeds the JupyterHub pod's 187 GiB cgroup limit. Architecture-level issue in 18_growclust_xc_prep.py , not a data bug.
SLURM job (preferred) — submit Stage 3 to a compute node with its own memory request. Zero code change, zero accuracy risk. Need to verify SLURM is configured on this hub first.
On-demand + LRU cache — replace preload_all_station_days with lazy loads inside the worker pool, cap at e.g. 2,000 entries. Same bytes read from same files; bit-identical XC. ~30 LOC change. Slower if eviction churns.
Disk-checkpoint cache — persist each loaded station-day to .npy , mmap on reuse. Float32 round-trip is bit-exact. Survives future pod restarts. More code, needs ~100s of GB scratch.
~/.claude/projects/-home-jovyan-bransfield-eq/memory/jupyterhub_pod_memory_limit.md
~/.claude/projects/-home-jovyan-bransfield-eq/memory/session_handoff_2026-05-13.md
Confirmed SLURM is not installed on this JupyterHub pod (no sbatch / sinfo ).
Patched scripts/18_growclust_xc_prep.py to drop preload_all_station_days and use a bounded LRU _WF_CACHE (OrderedDict, move_to_end on hit, popitem(last=False) on overflow). Added --cache-size CLI flag.
Also confirmed pod CPU cap = 32 cores ( /sys/fs/cgroup/cpu.max = 3200000/100000 ). Updated scripts/20_pipeline_finale.sh to --workers 32 and exported OMP/OPENBLAS/MKL/NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS=1 so each worker is single-threaded internally.
Launched 06:53; no anchor checkpoint logged in 31 min . Pod memory hit 185/187 GiB (99%).
py-spy was blocked by ptrace_scope=1 ; used /proc/<pid>/task/*/wchan instead — 3 threads in D state on wait_on_page_bit_common / do_user_addr_fault → page-cache thrashing . Process was forward-progressing in raw CPU terms but bouncing on disk for evicted page-cache.
Killed and relaunched with --cache-size 600 .
Launched 07:39. RSS dropped to ~46 GiB; but D-state threads on disk I/O went up to 7 (more re-reads).
Ran 4h 52min unattended → 150 / 36,757 anchors done. Effective rate ~0.01 anchors/sec. ETA ~1,000 hours (42 days) — won't finish.
Pod memory back at 184/187 GiB by hour 5 (page cache filling reclaimable but the run is still slow).
Each anchor pulls ~80 partner events; each partner needs ~5-10 station-day cache entries. With 32 threads working anchors in arbitrary order, the collective working set is thousands of unique station-days — neither cap (1500 or 600) holds them all hot. So LRU evicts entries that other threads are about to touch. Neither cache size fixes this.
Sort anchors by anchor-event origin time (or by spatial cluster + time) before submitting to the ThreadPoolExecutor. Adjacent-in-time anchors share station-days, giving the LRU real locality. Expected ~5-line change in main() of 18_growclust_xc_prep.py :
anchors = sorted(pairs_by_anchor.keys(),
 key=lambda i: events.iloc[i].origin_time)
Then 32 workers all stay roughly inside the same date window → cache hits dominate.

Update — date-sort fix tried (Run 3,  --cache-size 600  + anchor sort by origin time)
text:
Patched main() in scripts/18_growclust_xc_prep.py to (a) sort each anchor's partner list by partner origin time and (b) sort all anchors by anchor origin time before submitting to ThreadPoolExecutor . Idea was to give the LRU temporal locality so 32 threads stay inside a tight time window.
Measured first checkpoint: 50 anchors in 1435 s (~24 min) = 0.035 anchors/sec → ETA ~12 days . Compared to the unsorted run's ~42 days, that's a real 4× speedup — but still nowhere near usable. Rate further dropped to ~0.028/s by 53 min in.
Thread-state breakdown after sort fix: 28 R, 4 D (was 24 R, 7 D before sort) — confirms fewer threads stalling on disk page faults, but the underlying cost structure is the same.
Root cause confirmed at architectural level, not tuning level: _process_anchor re-decodes mseed inside the pair loop. Even with cache hits, every pick gets a fresh slice_window_from_array call (mean-subtract + L2-norm), and every cache miss pays a full obspy parse + resample. At ~30 partners × ~10 picks per anchor × 5–10 shared phases per pair, the per-anchor cost stays at ~36 s wall regardless of cache size or sort order.

text:
Cross-checked against published practice (EQcorrscan catalog_to_dd.write_correlations , hypoDDpy, QuakeSupport, the Rutford icequake catalog workflow). Universal pattern: pre-window every (event, station, phase) pick into a flat array, then XC the snippets — never decode mseed inside the pair loop.
Math justifying the pivot:
483,516 picks × (±1.5 s × 100 Hz × float32) = ~580 MB total . Fits in a single numpy.memmap .
Working-set reduction vs current station-day cache: ~50,000×. The 187 GiB pod cap becomes irrelevant.
Per-anchor cost drops from ~36 s (current measured) to ~0.3 s (theoretical: 300 array fetches + 150 FFT XCs of 300-sample windows). Realistic 50–100× speedup.
Expected total wall time: ~6–8 hours end-to-end (≈20 min parallel pre-window pass + ~6–7 h vectorized XC pass).
Implementation outline (committed kill of Run 3 first):
New script 
scripts/18b_prewindow_picks.py — pre-allocate growclust/picker_only/pick_windows.npy (memmap, shape [n_picks, 300] , float32). For each station-day file (parallel, 32 thread workers), load + resample once, then write each pick's ±1.5 s window into its row by pick_id . Workers touch disjoint rows → no locking. Also writes a sidecar pick_metadata.parquet with pick_id , event_idx , sta_key , phase , pick_time for the XC stage to index by.
Refactor 
scripts/18_growclust_xc_prep.py — replace the _get_wf + slice_window_from_array path with a direct pick_windows[pick_id] lookup. Keep the existing pair selection (5 km / 80-per-event already gets pair count to 1.1M; DBSCAN pre-clustering would only shave another ~30–50%, not worth it now). Vectorize FFT XC over batches of pairs sharing a (station, phase) where possible.

text:
Pod OOM (Run 1, cache 1500 / ~52 GiB). Pod hit 185 / 187 GiB within 30 min; 0 anchor checkpoints logged. dmesg empty (cgroup OOMs don't log to host kernel). memory.events.oom_kill = 0 after pod restart is misleading — the counter resets. Symptom was the "Server unavailable — restart it?" JupyterHub banner, same as the original crashes.
nohup
 does not survive pod death. Once the pod is OOM-killed by the cgroup, every process inside dies regardless of nohup / setsid . Only mitigations are out-of-pod (SLURM, etc.) or bounding in-process memory. SLURM was confirmed unavailable on this hub.
No swap. memory.swap.max = 0 → cgroup OOM fires immediately on the offending allocation when memory.max is exceeded. No grace period.
Page-cache thrashing (Run 1). Process anon RSS ~80 GiB + kernel file-cache ~115 GiB pushed total cgroup memory to 99% of cap. 3+ threads stuck in D state on wait_on_page_bit_common / do_user_addr_fault — threads forward-progressing in raw CPU terms but bouncing on disk for evicted page-cache pages.
ptrace_scope = 1
. py-spy dump --pid <pid> denied permission. No sudo. Fallback: /proc/<pid>/task/*/wchan to infer thread states.
Smaller cache didn't fix wall-clock (Run 2, cache 600 / ~20 GiB). RSS dropped from 80 GiB to 47 GiB, D-state went 3 → 7 (more re-reads, not fewer), and 150 / 36,757 anchors finished in 4 h 52 min → ETA ~42 days . Per-anchor cost was ~117 s.
Sort-by-origin-time helped, but not enough (Run 3, cache 600 + anchor sort). Real 4× speedup: first 50 anchors in 1435 s (~24 min) = 0.035 anchors/sec → ETA ~12 days. Rate then drifted to ~0.028/s. Still wall-clock-infeasible.
Architectural root cause: mseed parse + resample inside the pair loop, even with perfect caching. slice_window_from_array is called per (pick, partner) — ~300 calls per anchor — and every cache miss is a full obspy read() + resample() . No LRU tune can fix that.
memory.current
 is misleading. Includes reclaimable kernel page cache. Watching memory.current / memory.max overstates real pressure; what actually matters for OOM risk is RssAnon from /proc/<pid>/status .
Bash history truncated. Only the most recent ~10 commands survive in ~/.bash_history (JupyterHub login-shell config), so reconstructing how the failed runs were launched relied on log timestamps rather than command history.

sectionPath: Pyocto year finished, XC prep killed by pod OOM
text:
The pre-window vs front-load comparison (Jan-Mar 2019) revealed that even with bit-identical pair content (verified by canonical-sorted dt.cc diff: 115,217 pairs, 0 differing observation rows), the final relocations disagreed for ~23% of events (p95 |Δh| = 2.81 km, max 4.9 km).
Research into the GrowClust Fortran source ( SRC/growclust.f90 + SRC/stats_subs.f90 ) pinpointed the cause:
Main loop sorts pairs by rfactor = ngood * rgoodavg using INDEXX from stats_subs.f90 — the Numerical Recipes heapsort, which is not stable .
Ties in rfactor (common with OBS data: integer ngood counts × coarse mean CC) → sort tie-break order is the dt.cc input order.
Our XC kernel uses ThreadPoolExecutor.as_completed , so dt.cc pair-block order is thread-finish order → non-deterministic across runs .
Same data, different dt.cc order → different cluster topology → ~20-25% of events relocate differently. Not documented in the GrowClust paper, user guide, or GitHub issues.
Implication for the 30-day-vs-yearly comparison: the p95 |Δh| ≈ 2.84 km tail we saw is partly real science (yearly run has 3.6× more pairs adding constraints) and partly this non-determinism noise floor. We can't cleanly separate the two without deterministic dt.cc.
scripts/18_growclust_xc_prep.py 's write_dtcc now:
Iterates sorted(pairs) so pair blocks are always written in (id_a, id_b) order.
Sorts each block's observations by (station, phase) .
With this patch, two runs of Stages 3+4 on the same data should produce bit-identical relocations regardless of thread scheduling. (Verification re-run pending after the in-flight control experiment finishes.)

sectionTitle: GrowClust reproducibility — found the real cause of May-12-vs-today divergence
sectionPath: Pyocto year finished, XC prep killed by pod OOM
GrowClust reproducibility — found the real cause of May-12-vs-today divergence
text:
User pointed out that growclust/partial30days/dt.cc (the May 12 dt.cc) was still on disk. I had previously and incorrectly claimed it was overwritten. It was preserved along with its evlist.txt , stlist.txt , and run/ subdirectory.
Re-running Stage 3 (XC prep) on jan2019 today and canonical-content-diffing against May 12's dt.cc revealed:
Same 109,574 pair blocks in both files (0 only-in-A, 0 only-in-B).
But 100,286 of those pairs (91.5%) have differing observation values.
The differences are systematic: every observation on a given pair shifts by the same offset (e.g. 0.0096 s on pair (4946, 9340) -- the same shift on BRA20-P, BRA26-P, BRA26-S).
Same shift across all stations of one pair = the value of origin_a − origin_b for that pair. Confirmed by git show 57c92c9 (the only post-May-12 commit on this script):
- rows.append((pa.sta_key, pa.phase, pick_dt_obs, cc)) # May 12 (wrong)
+ tt_dt = pick_dt_obs - origin_dt
+ rows.append((pa.sta_key, pa.phase, tt_dt, cc)) # today (correct)
The May 12 dt.cc stored pick-time differentials instead of travel-time differentials. GrowClust expects tt_a − tt_b (travel-time differential) where tt = pick − origin ; May 12 left the origin-time difference baked into the dt values, contaminating the relative-position signal. Today's code subtracts it.
Implication: the May 12 30-day partial catalog ( catalogs/growclust_partial30days.csv , notes/figures/growclust_relocations.png ) is based on incorrect dt.cc values. It should be treated as superseded , not as a trusted reference. Today's runs are the correct baseline.
Three same-day Jan 2019 reruns confirm this:
| Run | Relocated | Top cluster | Identical to May 12 | p95 |Δh| vs May 12 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| May 12 partial30days | 5,036 | 2,556 | — | — |
| Today A (pre-window) | 5,046 | 2,963 | 56.8% | 2.72 km |
| Today B (front-load) | 5,051 | 2,842 | 56.6% | 2.71 km |
| Today C (re-make pre-window) | 5,050 | 2,899 | 56.7% | 2.80 km |
Today's three runs cluster together (~10-15% intra-day non-determinism) and consistently lean away from May 12 in the same direction -- if it were just non-determinism, today's three would scatter around May 12. They don't. The systematic offset is the dt accounting fix.
Pre-window vs front-load dt.cc canonical diff: bit-identical XC math (we verified this earlier).
Pre-window vs front-load relocation differences: GrowClust order non-determinism on identical pair content.
May 12 vs today relocation differences: dt accounting bug fix + GrowClust non-determinism on top.
Pre-windowing is exonerated; the open issues are (a) the unstable INDEXX heapsort in SRC/growclust.f90 (canonical-sort patch on write_dtcc is the fix, currently reverted on user request) and (b) the now-fixed dt accounting bug that contaminated May 12 only.
Final year-long relocated catalog produced and plotted; all comparison figures saved (with the older 30-day plots preserved untouched). 30-day plot should be retired — it's pre-fix data.
hypoDD CT-only Jan 2019 catalog produced. Next experiment: hypoDD --with-xc (uses GrowClust's dt.cc) for sub-sample-precision relative locations.
Canonicalization patch in write_dtcc is currently reverted at user request. Going forward we should re-apply it for paper-quality reproducibility, since the May-12 ordering is not the right reference anymore.
Open question for next session: re-run the full year on hypoDD (will need MAXEVE/MAXDATA budget verified for 42 k events; the array sizes are already bumped). Then compare GrowClust-year vs hypoDD-year relocations on the corrected dt.cc.

sectionPath: Session 2026-05-14 — hypoDD at scale: monolithic vs. pruned + sub-cluster
text:
Year-long hypoDD v2 run launched 2026-05-13 23:21 UTC. ph2dt produced 302 MB dt.ct on the 42,040-event catalog. Two hypoDD binaries running in parallel against it: picker_only (gold-standard): niter_ct=2 , NSET=3, full LSQR schedule.
picker_only_fast : niter_ct=1 , NSET=2.
Both used the v2-fixed pipeline (per-layer Vp/Vs via IMOD=1, calibrated PhaseNet-prob weights, station elevations from elevation_m , ph2dt MAXOBS=80, MAXDIST=100 km, NaT guard, depth-sanity post-filter).
Jan 2019 dry-run finished in 9 min and looked correct, so the v2 config was validated at small scale before scaling up.
After ~7 h elapsed (fast) and ~6 h (gold), neither run had produced an iteration banner. The hypoDD log was 4,930 lines of "negative depth" warnings from inside iteration 1, then nothing. Process states were healthy ( R , 99.9 % CPU, stable RSS). The LSQR had been chewing on cluster 1 (20,036 events × 8.5 M dt observations) for hours and had not finished its first matrix-vector product cycle. Extrapolating from "still iter 1 after 11 h" gave a finish window of 3-7 days.
subprocess.run had a 10,800 s (3 h) timeout. That was way too tight for year-long scale and killed the original gold-standard run cleanly mid-iteration. Patched: removed the timeout entirely. The fast run was still alive at the time -- to escape the same fate I kill -ed only its python parent, leaving the hypoDD binary orphaned to init (PPID=1). Wrote scripts/watch_and_finalize_fast.sh to wait on the orphaned PID and parse the reloc file when (if) it finished. Relaunched the gold-standard with the patched (no-timeout) script.
Drafted a focused question for seismologists who have run hypoDD at this scale. Got back three concrete recommendations:
Stock serial hypoDD on 20 k events / 8 M dt is genuinely not pleasant. Graph density (millions of sparse rows per LSQR iteration on an 80 k-unknown system) dominates beyond a certain event-pair count.
Partitioning is defensible -- but prefer event-pair graph partitioning (edge weights = number of dt obs, mean CC, distance, shared stations) with overlapping halos / bridge events rather than pure geographic chopping. Yano et al. used 1,257 grid squares for Japan.
No drop-in MPI hypoDD fork. relocDD-py and FDTCC cover XC generation, not the LSQR solver itself.
Concrete workflow the expert recommended: pruned global relocation first, then dense subcluster relocations.
After 11 h+ each with no progress past iteration 1, killed picker_only (PID 23679) and picker_only_fast (PID 22568). Memory freed cleanly.
Re-ran scripts/23_run_ph2dt.py --label picker_only_pruned with aggressive pruning:
MINWGHT=0.5 (was 0.2)
MINLNK=16 (was 8)
MINOBS=16 (was 8)
MAXOBS=60 (was 80)
MAXSEP=5 (unchanged)
Effect: 76× smaller dt.ct (302 MB → 4 MB), 38× fewer pairs (263 k → 6,872), 1,463 events selected for relocation. The 41,000 unselected events are weakly-coupled singletons that don't meet the strict MINLNK / MINOBS thresholds.

noteTitle: Session 2026-05-14 — hypoDD at scale: monolithic vs. pruned + sub-cluster
sectionPath: Session 2026-05-14 — hypoDD at scale: monolithic vs. pruned + sub-cluster
text:
1. Stage A's RMS is dramatically lower than every other run — 147 ms vs ~190-200 ms for every other catalog. That's the expected effect of a strict prune: by requiring MINLNK=16, MINOBS=16, MINWGHT=0.5 , only the highest-coupling pairs survive, and the LSQR converges to a much tighter fit. Stage A is essentially the "high-confidence skeleton" of the year-long catalog — 676 events at sub-100 ms TT-residual precision.
2. Both Stage B catalogs put the swarm centroid in essentially the same place (−62.42, −58.38), within ~100 m of each other and ~5 km southeast of the OBS array centre. Variant differences are in event-count (5,064 vs 3,579) and depth distribution (median 3.61 vs 3.78 km), not in the location of the swarm itself.
3. Stage B depth distributions are narrower than Jan 2019 v2's. Both Stage B variants have p5–p95 depth spans of ~4-5 km, vs Jan 2019 v2's 7 km span. The strict sub-region partitioning suppresses the long depth tail — events that would have been pulled into deep poorly-constrained positions in a global solve stay closer to the cluster centroid.
4. Stage B-jan2019 (variant) is 
more conservative than Stage B (Stage A-seeded): 3,579 events vs 5,064. That's because the variant used tighter regions (1.5 km max radius + 0.8 km buffer) vs 2.0 + 1.0 km. Per-region geometry is more compact, but ~30 % of events that the original Stage B included as bridge events fall outside every region's tighter radius in the variant. Trade-off: variant has more spatial purity, fewer events relocated. Not necessarily worse — depends on which question you're answering.
5. Both Stage B catalogs flag ~97 % of relocated events as physical (below seafloor depth). Jan 2019 v2 was only 92 % — the global-cluster solve pulled more events into shallow / above-seafloor positions. The Stage B partitioning is gentler on shallow events: they get located in the context of their immediate neighbours instead of being pulled toward the global swarm centroid. The 3 % residual "above seafloor" events in Stage B are the depth-sanity post-filter outliers.

noteTitle: Session 2026-05-14 — hypoDD at scale: monolithic vs. pruned + sub-cluster
sectionPath: Session 2026-05-14 — hypoDD at scale: monolithic vs. pruned + sub-cluster
text:
I attempted to compare same physical events across catalogs (Stage A vs Stage B, Stage B vs Stage B variant, GrowClust vs Stage B) by joining on hypoDD's id column. Those comparisons are currently invalid. Root cause: scripts/22_pyocto_to_hypodd_input.py assigns hypodd_id = row_index + 1 after reset_index on whatever pyocto subset it processes. So id=1 in the full-year run is a different physical event than id=1 in any sub_X run. The Stage B merge step ( scripts/26_merge_stage_b.py ) uses id to dedupe bridge events between sub-regions — meaning the "5,064 unique events" claim is likely an overcount of unique events, because the same pyocto event appearing in two sub-regions gets two different hypoDD ids and is not detected as a duplicate.
Fix for next session: change line 58 of scripts/22_pyocto_to_hypodd_input.py from
ev["hypodd_id"] = (ev.index + 1).astype(int)
to
ev["hypodd_id"] = (ev["event_idx"] + 1).astype(int)
then re-run scripts 22, 23, 24 for all Stage B sub-regions and re-merge. Final event counts will drop (real duplicates will collapse) but the catalog is then correctly indexed and cross-catalog comparison becomes meaningful.
For now we can only claim within-catalog stats are valid. The depth distributions, RMS residuals, and swarm geometry are correct; the event-count totals are an upper bound.
Combining the three valid within-catalog observations:
Swarm centroid: (−62.425 ± 0.005°, −58.385 ± 0.005°) — ~5 km SSE of the OBS array centre, at the location of the previously-mapped Orca seamount.

High-confidence skeleton (Stage A): 676 events that pass strict double-difference linking. These are the events you should trust for absolute relative positions and depth structure interpretation.
